clock.title: NTP synchronization
clock.lede: PyAutomation verifies the system clock against plant NTP servers. Clock discipline is done by chrony on the host; this panel only monitors compliance. No environment variables are required — configure everything here.
clock.statusHint: Latest edge clock check against the configured plant NTP servers.
clock.bannerMetaIdle: No recent check or no servers configured
clock.hostTimeNote: Clock discipline is handled by the OS (chrony). This panel only verifies. Check times are shown in UTC; the HMI may use {{zone}} on other screens.
clock.configHint: Changes persist in the service and apply immediately. Admins only.
clock.serversHint: Use an IPv4/IPv6 address or DNS hostname for each server. Separate multiple servers with commas.
clock.serversTooltip: SNTP over UDP 123. Compatible with Linux (chrony/ntpd) and Windows Server (w32time) when the NTP service is enabled and port 123 is open. No credentials required. If the server requires authentication, the monitor will report it and will not work until you use an unauthenticated server.
clock.authRequired: The NTP server requires authentication. This is not supported yet. Use an unauthenticated server or wait for a future release with symmetric/NTS support.
clock.stepDetected: A sharp clock step (> configured threshold) was detected on the last check.
clock.intervalHint: Between 60 s and 24 h. Typical plant value: 3600 s (1 h).
clock.failClosedHint: Pause acquisition when clock exceeds alarm threshold
clock.saveNote: Save applies servers, interval, and thresholds without restarting the service.
clock.adminOnly: Only administrators can edit NTP settings.
